plan_fit.method: Each official floor-plan image (S2-S6) was registered to the OSM footprint with a piecewise-linear x and y mapping through wall lines that match OSM edges (NE tower top/right/bottom, NE notch, east and south walls, SW tower, SW loading-dock notch, west wing). Wall lines were found by scanning the images for long dark runs. An overlay of the OSM outline on every plan agreed to about +-1 m on floors 1, 2, 4 and 5; floor 3's drawing compresses its west half (about +-2 m there).
findings: Setbacks are whole 30-ft modules: the 4th floor's east wall measures -43.3 (OSM notch line -42.6; one module in from the east wall = -42.68) and its south wall -115.7 (OSM loading-dock line -115.9; one module = -115.86). The 5th floor's east wall measures -51.9 (two modules = -51.83); its south wall -108.1 lines up with the SW tower's north face (-107.8).
The 3rd-floor atrium opening measures X -60.8..-52.5, Y -97.9..-106.3, i.e. exactly the module cell X -60.97..-51.83, Y -106.71..-97.57 (the 30-ft-square atrium of S10).

Floors 2 and 3 stop at Y -75.9 / -74.4 on the north wing while floors 4-5 reach the OSM line -69.0: a two-storey covered porch about 6 m deep in front of the north doors (OSM has covered picnic tables there).
The basement's North Computer Lab runs about 17 m north of the OSM outline (to Y -52.5), under the court roof and the south end of the CSE building.
The elevators sit at about (-72.6, -89.7) on every floor, with their doors facing south; the fish tank (S4/S14) is about 6 m south of them.

hub_followups: The real main doors are at X -69.2..-65.2 in a wall recessed to Y -75.5 under a two-storey porch; hub door 4 is at (-58.5, -69.0) on the OSM line. Optional: move the hub door 8.7 m west and recess it (flow.md 4.1 would change).

The plans put the stepped terraces on the south-east (floor 4 set back one module on the east and south, floor 5 two modules east and to the SW-tower line on the south). The hub model steps the north wing instead and keeps a flat 16.8 m roof over the SE.
Floors 2-3 are recessed about 6.5 m on the north wing (two-storey porch); the hub model has a single-storey colonnade on the west only.
The zig-zag glass bays face the court (NW diagonal), stacked over the court doors (photo S20); the hub skylight 'in the middle' has no source but happens to sit over the game atrium, so keep it.
open_questions: Real floor-to-floor height (4.2 m assumed; 4.5 m is also typical for 1980s libraries with compact shelving).
Grade on the west: is the basement at grade with the Marston Courtyard bowl (three west exits on S2, vending machines tagged level -1 near the French Fries)?
Whether the SE terraces carry sloped glazing or planting, and whether anyone can walk on them.
Number of passenger elevators (one symbol per floor on the plans; two assumed).
Location of the data consultation room (floor 3) and the real floor accent colours.
Whether the North Computer Lab really runs ~17 m north under CSE (the 1st-floor plan says so; nothing else confirms it).
